```{r}
# ============================================================
# Setup
# ============================================================
if (!requireNamespace("h2o", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("h2o")
library(h2o)
if (!requireNamespace("h2o", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("h2o")
library(mlbench)

h2o.init(nthreads = -1, max_mem_size = "4G")

# Load dataset
data(PimaIndiansDiabetes2, package = "mlbench")
df <- na.omit(PimaIndiansDiabetes2)  # remove NAs

# Convert to H2O frame
df_h2o <- as.h2o(df)
x <- setdiff(names(df), "diabetes")
y <- "diabetes"
df_h2o[, y] <- as.factor(df_h2o[, y])

# ============================================================
# Run AutoML with internal cross-validation
# ============================================================
aml <- h2o.automl(
  x = x,
  y = y,
  training_frame = df_h2o,
  nfolds = 5,              # 5-fold cross-validation
  max_models = 10,         # number of models to try
  max_runtime_secs = 60,   # quick example
  seed = 1234
)

# ============================================================
# Inspect leaderboard with CV metrics
# ============================================================
# The leaderboard by default shows leaderboard-frame metrics,
# but we can request CV-based metrics directly:
lb <- h2o.get_leaderboard(aml, extra_columns = "ALL")
print(lb)

# ============================================================
# Extract and inspect cross-validation performance for each model
# ============================================================
model_ids <- as.data.frame(lb$model_id)[,1]

cv_results <- lapply(model_ids, function(id) {
  m <- h2o.getModel(id)
  perf <- m@model$cross_validation_metrics_summary
  auc <- as.numeric(perf["auc","mean"])
  acc <- as.numeric(perf["accuracy","mean"])
  data.frame(model = id, AUC = auc, Accuracy = acc)
})

cv_results_df <- do.call(rbind, cv_results)
cv_results_df <- cv_results_df[order(-cv_results_df$AUC), ]
print(cv_results_df)

# ============================================================
# Visualize CV performance
# ============================================================
if (requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)) {
  library(ggplot2)
  ggplot(cv_results_df, aes(x = reorder(model, AUC), y = AUC)) +
    geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
    coord_flip() +
    labs(title = "Cross-validated AUC across H2O models",
         x = "Model", y = "AUC (5-fold CV)")
}

# ============================================================
# Shutdown (optional)
# ============================================================
# h2o.shutdown(prompt = FALSE)

```

Survival
```{r}
# ============================================================
# Cox Proportional Hazards in H2O (Survival Analysis)
# Works on versions requiring both start and stop columns
# ============================================================
if (!requireNamespace("h2o", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("h2o")
library(h2o)
library(survival)

h2o.init(nthreads = -1, max_mem_size = "4G")

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Load and prepare dataset
# ------------------------------------------------------------
data(lung)
lung <- na.omit(lung)
lung$sex <- as.factor(lung$sex)
lung$status <- ifelse(lung$status == 2, 1, 0)  # 1 = event

# Create required start/stop columns for H2O Cox model
lung$start <- 0
lung$stop  <- lung$time

# Convert to H2O frame
lung_h2o <- as.h2o(lung)

# Define predictors and survival columns
x <- setdiff(names(lung), c("start", "stop", "status", "time"))
start_col <- "start"
stop_col  <- "stop"
event_col <- "status"

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Fit CoxPH model
# ------------------------------------------------------------
cox_model <- h2o.coxph(
  x = x,
  training_frame = lung_h2o,
  start_column = start_col,
  stop_column = stop_col,
  event_column = event_col
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Evaluate C-index on training data
# ------------------------------------------------------------
perf <- h2o.performance(cox_model, train = TRUE)
c_index <- h2o.concordance(perf)

cat("\nCoxPH Concordance Index (C-index) on full dataset:", round(c_index, 3), "\n")

```
